profile.owner: Independent, privately held Utah company (Provo/Spanish Fork), founded 2011 by Jeremiah Olsen and Scott Hunter. No parent company or acquisition found. GetLatka estimates about 8 employees.
profile.target_customers: Small to mid-sized residential pest control operators, especially door-to-door sales driven companies. Price tiers run to about 500 active recurring customers, with custom quotes above that.
profile.pricing: Monthly tiers by active recurring customer count, unlimited users, no long-term contract. G2 (vendor provided): Starter $59 (0-20 customers), Scale Light $109 (21-50), Large $159 (51-300), Larger $225 (300-500), custom above. Other sites quote higher figures ($99 to $275) and a $300 setup fee. Extras per help center: SMS $3 to $4 per number per month plus $0.03 to $0.04 per text; Find My Tech GPS and time clock $9 to $19 per tech per month. Pricing is not shown in fetchable form on pocomos.com.
profile.deployment: Cloud. Responsive web app for the office plus native iOS and Android apps for technicians and sales reps.
profile.mobile_app: Pocomos Tech App (iOS App Store) and Pocomos mobile app (Google Play), used by technicians, owners and door-to-door sales reps.
integrations: QuickBooks Online (one-way nightly sync of customers, invoices and paid payments)
SendJim (direct mail postcards and drip campaigns, US only)
In-house card, debit and ACH processing (help center references Zift, Bottom Line Payments and CardConnect)
Sales tax rate database (zip code based rates)
Podium and Birdeye listed by vendor as in progress
strengths: Support is consistently praised in reviews as fast and helpful
Simple, easy to learn routing and drag-and-drop scheduling with an advanced optimizer included in every plan
Low entry price with unlimited users, priced by active customers
Strong door-to-door sales tooling: leads map, sales teams, leaderboards, commissions, recruiting and a video training platform
Paperless agreements signed in person or remotely, plus estimates with e-signature approval
weaknesses: Reviewers describe the interface as dated or boxy
Limited reporting depth (retention is calculated manually from a delinquent report)
Customer portal called primitive by a reviewer, with payment link problems; no self-scheduling
Required in-house card processing seen as expensive by some users; few integrations and no documented API
Common add-on costs (GPS tracking, time clock, SMS) and per-customer tiers that shift as customer counts fluctuate
profile.wisconsin_notes: No Wisconsin customers or Wisconsin-specific compliance found. No mention of ATCP 29 records, the landscape registry, posting signs or state regulatory reports. Compliance support is generic: chem sheets, dilution rates and per-service technician license numbers.

features.notes: Leads module with leads map, lead lists and conversion to customers. Sales statuses drive commissions; no documented stage-based sales pipeline.
Marketing type recorded on each customer to track where business comes from. Reports on close rate or revenue by source not documented.
Enhanced Estimates: unlimited line items, optional and recommended items, sent by email PDF or SMS link. No named good, better, best tiers.
Agreements signed on device at the door or remotely by emailed link; estimates can also be approved with a signature.
Door-to-door tools: leads map, My Spots time slots for reps, sales teams, leaderboard and sign-up from mobile. Knock tracking detail not documented.
Commission amounts set per salesperson and technician; sales statuses decide which accounts qualify. Holds or chargebacks on early cancellation not documented.
Mass email and text, scheduled emails and job-triggered messages exist. Automated drip sequences only via SendJim direct mail, not email or SMS.
Configurable cancel reasons chosen on cancellation, visible in the Delinquent Report. No save-attempt or retention workflow documented.
Parent account with child sub-locations for landlords and property managers, managed under one account.
No click-to-call, call tracking or caller ID pop documented. A reviewer noted no automated calling.
Recurring agreements from weekly to custom frequencies; multiple agreements per customer allowed.
No documentation of seasonal programs or fixed rounds within a date window.
Service types carry default pricing and descriptions; products, line items and default discount types exist. Pricing by property size or tier not documented.
Bulk Modify Contract Pricing by percent, flat amount or new price, with a Price Increase Report. Per-service and monthly contracts only.
Contracts auto-renew and create new jobs after the last job completes. Term length settings and early cancellation fees not documented.
No warranty tracking or warranty renewal billing found in public docs.
No re-service or callback tracking with cost capture found in public docs.
Creating a contract generates its scheduled jobs, which feed the job pool for routing; renewals generate the next set overnight.
Redesigned Calendar and Job Pool with drag-and-drop routing plus a Route Map view.
Advanced route optimizer handles up to 1,000 jobs, with selectable start points; included in all plans per G2 pricing.
Qualified Technicians flags which techs can do each service type, but only warns and does not block assignment.
Portal shows upcoming services and payments only; no booking. Reviewers request customer self-scheduling.
Find My Tech live and historical tech location is paid per tech per month ($9 to $19 by ping frequency).
Vendor overview lists mass job adjustments; help center covers moving an entire route and bulk completing jobs.
Pocomos Tech App on iOS and Android for technicians, owners and sales reps.
Vendor overview says technicians can work offline and sync later; G2 pricing also lists offline tech apps.
Chem sheets in the app record products, dilution and application rates, with auto-fill templates and product blends.
App captures photos, notes, checklists and customer signatures.
Device tracking and app docs do not mention barcode scanning.
Techs receive payments and add payment accounts in the app, subject to permissions.
Clock in through the tech app with a Time Clock report and CSV export, but it requires the paid Find My Tech feature.
No truck or vehicle stock on the device documented; app article covers product setup only.
Job chem sheets capture product, amount, dilution and application type. No state-specific application record format documented.
Central product list with dilution rates, distributor and low-stock threshold. EPA numbers, label and SDS documents not documented.
License number stored per technician per service type requiring a license. No expiry alerts or certification categories documented.
Chemical usage reports exist, but no reports formatted for state regulators found.
Generic automatic email or SMS sent a set time before scheduled jobs could serve as notice; no pesticide-specific notices.
No restricted-use pesticide controls or RUP record fields found.
Basic product inventory with low-level thresholds and distributor. Warehouse or branch stock, purchasing and transfers not documented.
Vendor does not mention Wisconsin, ATCP 29, landscape registry notice or posting signs.
Optional Device Tracking module tracks traps and bait stations per property with device types and inspection questions. Barcodes not mentioned.
Devices shown as pins on an aerial property view; no floor plan or facility diagram documented.
Inspection details print on invoices; no per-device activity history or trend reports found.
No AIB, SQF, BRC or other food safety audit reporting found.
Portal lets customers download invoices and share uploaded files. No service reports, device maps, labels or SDS documented.
No customer sighting log or corrective action tracking found.
PO numbers print on invoices and multi-location invoices can combine into one bill. Net terms not documented.
No termite graphs, bait monitoring workflow or WDI reports found.
No wildlife trapping or exclusion job workflow found.
Technician checklists exist, but no bed bug multi-visit or customer prep checklist workflow found.
No lawn care programs, measurements or fertilizer rounds found.
No seasonal mosquito or tick program features found.
Credit, debit and ACH processed inside Pocomos through its processor; some reviewers say the required processor is costly.
Cards, debit and ACH stored on file, multiple per account, with autopay.
Per-service and monthly billing contracts, plus prepay via Due at Signup or charging multiple future invoices.
Zip code based tax rates from a tax database and tax codes per customer. Taxability per service type not documented.
Automatic invoice alerts by email or SMS after due date and collections agency export. Late fees, retries and service holds not documented.
Multiple invoices can combine into one bill, and unpaid billing summaries can be printed or sent.
No automatic proration or cancellation balance logic found; refunds are processed manually.
No general ledger in docs; accounting is handled by pushing customers, invoices and payments one way to QuickBooks Online.
One-way nightly sync to QuickBooks Online. QuickBooks Desktop support not documented.
No Sage, Xero, NetSuite or other accounting integration found.
Prepayments mark future invoices paid; no deferred revenue recognition documented.
No labor and material job costing or margin reporting found.
Technician and sales commissions with reports, and time clock CSV export (paid add-on). No payroll integration documented.
Portal shows upcoming services, pays invoices one at a time, stores payment methods. No service requests; reviewers report link problems.
Automatic email or SMS reminders before scheduled jobs, and one-tap En Route texts from the tech app.
Two-way SMS with history and unanswered message report; $4 per number monthly plus $0.04 per text.
Automatic review requests after job completion through the Opiniion integration, which needs its own account.
Completed job invoice is emailed with products used, optional photos and device inspection details.
Dashboards plus AR, revenue, commissions, chemical usage, cancellation and tax reports.
Retention is calculated by hand from the Delinquent Report; no breakdown by route, tech or service documented.
Technician dashboard, commission reports and reporting by technician. Time on site and re-service rates not documented.
Advanced search and customer data export to file; no user-built report designer or BI connector found.
Multiple branches with one corporate login, cross-branch dashboards and roll-up reporting.
Five default roles with individually adjustable permissions per role and per employee.
No public API, webhooks or Zapier connector found.
Onboarding articles cover setup steps but do not mention vendor-led data import from prior software.
No AI features advertised; Recommend Customers route fill is described as rule-based.
No hosted website or embeddable lead or booking forms found.
Direct mail to neighbors, leads and customers through the SendJim integration (US only). No call tracking or SEO.

extra_features.notes: Built-in recruiting tools for hiring door-to-door sales reps, included in all plans per G2.
Hosts custom sales and technician training videos with certification levels and a video usage report.
Top 20 leaderboard, sales dashboards and automatic alerts when reps make sales or hit milestones.
Clicking an open route slot ranks due customers by least added drive time to fill gaps.
Suggests best slots when creating or rescheduling customers, with filters.
Configurable checklists technicians complete on jobs.
Local weather data captured on service records in the tech app.
Physical invoices mailed singly or in bulk through a central mailer.
Internal alerts, pop-up account notes techs must clear, and company bulletin.
Pays only for accounts with an upcoming service; every plan allows unlimited users.
